subject: Follow-up: PulseBridge POC — data retention carveout and next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@pulsebridge.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: PulseBridge POC — data retention carveout and next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the PulseBridge POC scope and the data-handling asks you raised.

Recap of key asks from your side:
- 0-retention for user PII/PHI tokens (they cannot be persisted in any logs or KV cache)
- Shortened operational logs for non-PII telemetry (proposed range 7–14 days)
- US-only data residency for model inference and logs
- Evidence: SOC 2 and a sample audit log showing purge workflow
- Ability to scope which API routes send PII vs non-PII

Internal asks / what I need from you now:
1) Can you confirm which endpoints will send PII vs non-PII (list of routes) by EOD Thursday?
2) Procurement timeline — you mentioned a Nov 10 target to sign the POC SOW; is that still accurate?
3) Any special redline requirements for security addendum? You referenced a short clause about not persisting PHI.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- We will circulate two technical options by end-of-week: (A) Scoped 0-retention for PII + 7-day operational logs (hosted) and (B) 0-retention + 14-day logs with Dedicated capacity (for stronger isolation).
- Aditya and Lauren will validate engineering impacts and any performance/SLO tradeoffs.
- If you want the strictest guarantee, we will surface Private deployment requirements (timeline & cost).

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf (high-level options) and pulsebridge-poc-mvp-requirements.xlsx (what you shared on the call).

If that aligns, I’ll aim to get a proposal out by Friday and we can schedule a 30-minute technical review next week.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park

From: Samir Gupta <samir@pulsebridge.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PulseBridge POC — data retention carveout and next steps

Kim, thanks for the recap and quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Endpoints: We’ll send a definitive list of routes that will carry PII by Thursday; preliminary list attached to this reply.
2) Retention: Our compliance team requires absolute 0-retention for any PHI-containing tokens (we store PHI in our database; the inference path must not persist PHI). For non-PII logs (metrics, latency, errors without content) we can accept 7 days, ideally extendable to 14 if needed for debugging during ramp.
3) Residency: US-only is a must for this POC.
4) Procurement: Nov 10 is still the target for SOW signature, but we need the exact technical concession documented for legal (they want plain language we can pass to procurement).

I’ve attached "redlined_requirements.pdf" with the wording our security team prefers for the PHI clause — please review and let me know if this is implementable with Hosted or if Dedicated/Private is required.

Also: can Redwood provide a short statement on how KV caching is handled during inference and whether we can disable prefix caching on sensitive routes?

Appreciate the help — Samir

--
Samir Gupta
Head of Ops, PulseBridge
samir@pulsebridge.io | +1 (212) 555-0188
Attachment: redlined_requirements.pdf (1 page)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-14T14:36:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: PulseBridge POC — options for PII/retention carveout (internal)

Kim / Lauren — quick engineering read on options and operational impact. I’ll follow up with an RFC if we need Private. Summary below:

Options (tradeoffs):
A) Hosted Scoped 0-retention + 7-day non-PII logs
   - Implementation: route-level flag to disable persisting input and disable prefix KV caching for flagged routes; on-the-fly redaction for obvious PHI patterns; per-request bypass of trace capture.
   - Pros: fastest to deliver, lower cost.
   - Cons: harder guaranteed isolation; auditors may push back on "zero persistence" without Private deploy evidence.

B) Hosted 0-retention + 14-day non-PII logs (buffer for debugging)
   - Same as A but with longer retention for operational artifacts.

C) Dedicated / Private with enforced ephemeral-mode for PII routes
   - Full isolation, can disable all disk persistence and run in ephemeral RAM-forwarding for those routes.
   - Pros: clearest compliance posture, easier to provide audit evidence.
   - Cons: cost increase + longer lead time (provisioning).

My recommendation for a POC: Start with option A (Hosted scoped 0-retention) but include an explicit fallback path to C if legal requires hardware isolation. Provide a clear artifact set: 1) config snippet showing route-level flag, 2) sample purge/runbook, 3) SOC 2 report and a short audit evidence pack. I can draft the config snippet and an SLO note (expected latency delta <5% for flagged routes).

Next technical questions for Samir (we should include in the reply):
- Which exact fields in the request payload should be treated as PII/PHI (field names)?
- Do you require cryptographic attestation (HSM/KMS) for key management on POC data?

Attachments: retention-options-2026-10-14.docx (internal notes).

Aditya
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@pulsebridge.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: scoped 0-retention + operational logs (options & next steps)

Samir — appreciate the quick clarifications and the redline from your team. Per Aditya’s engineering read, here are two concrete options for the POC and what we will deliver to document compliance. Please review and let me know which you prefer so we can lock the SOW language for procurement.

Offer A (Fast path, Hosted):
- Scoped 0-retention for designated PII/PHI routes (route-level flag; input payloads for flagged fields not written to logs or KV cache).
- Non-PII operational logs retained for 7 days (extendable to 14 on request).
- US-only residency for inference and logs.
- Deliverables: config snippet + runbook, SOC 2 report, sample purge log, short technical attestation (1 page).
- Estimated time to enable: 4 business days after list of routes/fields.
- Cost: standard hosted POC pricing.

Offer B (Stronger isolation, Dedicated/Private):
- All of Offer A plus Dedicated capacity or Private deployment with enforced ephemeral mode for PII routes (no disk persistence).
- Deliverables: above + provisioning ETA and an HSM/KMS integration note if requested.
- Estimated time to enable: 3–4 weeks (provisioning + validation).
- Additional costs apply.

Action items from PulseBridge to proceed:
1) Confirm preferred offer (A or B).
2) Provide definitive list of routes and field names to treat as PII by Thursday 10/16.
3) Confirm if you require HSM-backed attestation for keys.

If you accept Offer A, we’ll slot a 30-minute technical review on Monday to sample the config and confirm the purge workflow; I’ll attach a short SOW paragraph that legal/procurement can drop into the POC SOW. I’ll also include a DocuSign link for the minimal POC addendum once you confirm.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/claim/ABC123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4921

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in so your team can start the POC on schedule.

Best,
Kim
